document_title: Code of Medical Ethics
notes: Current edition with 9 Principles + Council Opinions. First promulgated 1847; continuously updated. Widely adopted by state medical boards though not legally binding.

document_title: WMA International Code of Medical Ethics
notes: 2022 major revision (4-year process); first adopted 1949. Adds provisions on environmental health, remote care, physician well-being.

document_title: WMA Declaration of Geneva — Physician's Pledge
notes: Modern Hippocratic Oath; first adopted 1948. 2017 revision was the largest update in decades, adding patient autonomy, physician self-care, medical knowledge sharing.

document_title: CMA Code of Ethics and Professionalism
notes: Updated 2018; one of profession's most important documents since 1868. Based on compassion, beneficence, non-maleficence, respect for persons, justice, accountability.

document_title: Good Medical Practice
notes: Effective January 30, 2024. Statutory regulator. Covers doctors, physician associates, and anaesthesia associates. 11 categories of professional standards.

document_title: Core Ethics Guidance
notes: Updated February 2025. Practical guidance (not rules) for ethical decision-making. Covers confidentiality, consent, children, mental capacity. Complementary to GMC standards.

document_title: Declaration of Professional Responsibility: Medicine's Social Contract with Humanity
notes: Adopted December 4, 2001. 9 duties transcending specialties. Drafted partly in response to September 11; addresses medicine's role in public health and global responsibilities.

document_title: Statement on Principles (Code of Professional Conduct)
notes: Originally 1913 (anti-fee-splitting focus); revised 1974, 2004, 2016. Covers Code of Professional Conduct, qualifications, surgeon-patient relationship, discrimination prohibition.

organization: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists
document_title: Code of Professional Ethics
notes: Foundational principle: welfare of patient forms basis of all medical judgments. Multiple committee opinions supplement the core ethics code.

document_title: Code of Ethics for Nurses with Interpretive Statements
notes: Released January 29, 2025. 10 provisions (new 10th provision on global ethical issues added). Previous version was 2015. Nursing's ethical standard of practice and social contract.

document_title: ICN Code of Ethics for Nurses
notes: First adopted 1953; revised 2021 reflecting COVID-19 lessons. 4-element structure: nurses & people, nurses & practice, nurses & coworkers, nurses & profession.

document_title: The Code: Professional Standards of Practice and Behaviour for Nurses, Midwives and Nursing Associates
notes: October 2018 version current. Required for UK registration. 4 themes: prioritise people, practise effectively, preserve safety, promote professionalism and trust.

document_title: Code of Members' Professional Values and Behaviour
notes: Applies to all RCN members. Complementary to NMC Code. Emphasizes maintaining professional reputation, respect, confidentiality.

organization: National Association of Directors of Nursing Administration in Long Term Care
document_title: NADONA Code of Ethics
notes: Covers nursing administration in LTC settings. Supports quality of care for individuals receiving and delivering long-term care.

document_title: Principles of Ethics and Code of Professional Conduct
notes: March 2023 version current. Three-part structure: Principles of Ethics (aspirational), Code of Professional Conduct (binding), Advisory Opinions. 5 fundamental principles: autonomy, nonmaleficence, beneficence, justice, veracity.

document_title: Standards for the Dental Team
notes: Effective September 30, 2013. 9 principles for all dental team members. Failure may result in fitness to practise proceedings and removal from GDC Register.

document_title: ADHA Code of Ethics
notes: Adopted October 2024. Specific to dental hygienists.

document_title: Code of Ethics for Pharmacists
notes: Established 1852; most recent revision 1994. 8 principles based on moral obligations and virtues. Covers covenantal relationship, compassion, autonomy, justice.

document_title: Statement of Professional Standards: Codes of Ethics for Pharmacists
notes: FIP Council approved 2014. Adopted by professional organizations in 91 countries. Oath/promise available in 18 languages. Covers autonomy, beneficence, non-maleficence, justice.

document_title: Standards for Pharmacy Professionals
notes: 9 standards applicable in all practice settings. UK statutory regulator for pharmacists and pharmacy technicians in Great Britain. Updated patient safety standards April 2024.

document_title: Professional Standards for Hospital Pharmacy Services
notes: First published 2012; 2017 version current. Covers acute, mental health, private, community, hospice, ambulance settings. Multiple domain-specific professional standards documents.

document_title: Code of Ethics for the Physical Therapist
notes: 2020 version current. July 2025 APTA House of Delegates adopted new unified Code of Ethics for Physical Therapy Profession (combining PT and PTA standards), effective January 1, 2026.

document_title: Ethical Principles for Physical Therapists
notes: Formerly WCPT; in official relations with WHO since 1952. Represents 600,000+ physiotherapists through 129 member organizations. Ethical Principles define professional duties globally.

document_title: Code of Members' Professional Values and Behaviour
notes: 2019 revision. 4 core principles: taking responsibility for actions, behaving ethically, delivering effective service, striving for excellence. Applies to all roles and career stages.

document_title: Standards of Conduct, Performance and Ethics
notes: Effective September 1, 2024. UK statutory regulator for 15+ allied health professions including physiotherapists, OTs, radiographers, speech therapists, dietitians, paramedics, psychologists. 7 core standards.

document_title: 2025 Occupational Therapy Code of Ethics
notes: 2025 edition (previous was 2020). 7 core values + 6 guiding principles: beneficence, non-maleficence, autonomy, justice, veracity, fidelity. First formal code established 1975.

document_title: WFOT Guiding Principles for Ethical Occupational Therapy
notes: 2024 update (replaced 2016 Code of Ethics). 101 national OT organizations represented. Endorses UN Universal Declaration of Human Rights. Serves as guide for member associations.

document_title: ASHA Code of Ethics
notes: First established 1952; regularly updated. Covers Certificate of Clinical Competence holders and members. Requires 1 CEU ethics hour per 3-year certification cycle.

organization: Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics / Commission on Dietetic Registration
document_title: Code of Ethics for the Nutrition and Dietetics Profession
profession_name: Registered Dietitian Nutritionist/Nutrition and Dietetic Technician
notes: Effective June 1, 2018. Joint Academy/CDR document. Reviewed codes of 11 professional associations. 4 moral principles: non-maleficence, autonomy, beneficence, justice.

organization: American Society of Radiologic Technologists / American Registry of Radiologic Technologists
document_title: Code of Ethics / Standards of Ethics
notes: Joint ASRT/ARRT ethical framework. ARRT Standards of Ethics 2020. Covers competence, patient care, confidentiality, non-discrimination, continuing education.

document_title: Statement of Ethics and Professional Conduct
notes: AARC position statement. Defines basic ethical and moral standards. Covers integrity, competence, patient rights, privacy, non-discrimination, anti-fraud provisions.

document_title: Ethical Principles of Psychologists and Code of Conduct
notes: 2002 code; 2010 and 2017 amendments. 5 General Principles (aspirational) + enforceable Ethical Standards. Widely adopted by state licensing boards. Draft 2024/2025 revision in progress.

document_title: The Principles of Medical Ethics with Annotations Especially Applicable to Psychiatry
notes: Annotates AMA Principles with psychiatric-specific guidance. First psychiatric-specific ethics code adopted 1970 in response to public concerns. Covers confidentiality, boundary violations, informed consent. Includes Goldwater Rule.

document_title: ACA Code of Ethics
notes: 2014 revision. Expanded guidance on technology, social media, distance counseling, multicultural considerations. 6 fundamental ethical principles. Widely used across counseling specialties.

document_title: NBCC Code of Ethics
notes: Approved May 2023, revised August 2023. 114 ethical standards in 6 areas including telemental health, social media, technology. Largest national counselor credentialing body.

organization: American Association for Marriage and Family Therapy
document_title: AAMFT Code of Ethics
notes: Revised AAMFT Code of Ethics effective January 1, 2026. Core values include equity, belonging, mutual respect, diversity. Enforced by AAMFT Ethics Committee.

organization: International Association of Marriage and Family Counselors
document_title: IAMFC Code of Ethics
notes: Adopted 2017; published 2018. Division of the American Counseling Association. 10 sections covering all aspects of couple and family counseling including multicultural inclusion.

organization: NAADAC — The Association for Addiction Professionals / National Certification Commission for Addiction Professionals
document_title: NAADAC/NCCAP Code of Ethics
notes: 2021 update (previous revision 2016). Covers full continuum: prevention, intervention, treatment, recovery support. Required by many state certification boards. Guiding values: fidelity, loyalty, diligence, discretion, non-maleficence.

organization: National Association of Emergency Medical Technicians
document_title: EMS Code of Ethics
notes: Originally drafted by Charles Gillespie MD in 1978; first revised June 14, 2013. 6 core principles: professionalism, respect, integrity, compassion, accountability, excellence. Patient-centered update.

document_title: Code of Ethics and Standards of Professional Conduct
notes: Three-document suite: Code of Ethics, Optometric Oath, Standards of Professional Conduct (adopted June 2011). Standards organized under 4 bioethical principles (autonomy, non-maleficence, beneficence, justice).

document_title: Standards of Practice for Optometrists and Dispensing Opticians
notes: 19 standards of behaviour. UK statutory regulator for optical professions. College of Optometrists provides supplementary Guidance for Professional Practice (2023 edition).

document_title: Code of Ethics
notes: Based on primary responsibility to benefit the patient. Addresses excellence, professional conduct, sexual misconduct prohibition, anti-abandonment, healthcare collaboration.

document_title: Code of Ethics
notes: 2017 version. APMA members obligated to follow as part of membership. Addresses patient safety supervision, conflict of interest, gifts/gratuities, fraud prevention.

document_title: Code of Ethics with Explanatory Statements
notes: Foundation document for midwifery practice in US. Emphasizes human rights, dignity, autonomy, justice. Covers practice, research, education responsibilities. AMCB references ACNM code for discipline.

document_title: International Code of Ethics for Midwives
notes: Established 1993; revised and re-confirmed 1999 at ICM Council in Manila. 4 sections: midwifery relationships, practice, professional responsibilities, advancement of knowledge.

document_title: Public Health Code of Ethics
notes: Effective November 2019; replaced 2002 code. Not disciplinary; provides ethical framework. Emphasizes social justice, equity, community health. First national public health ethics code was APHA's 2002 adoption.

document_title: WHO Global Code of Practice on the International Recruitment of Health Personnel
notes: Adopted at 63rd World Health Assembly 2010; reviewed 2023. Ethical principles for international health personnel recruitment. Aims to protect health systems of developing countries.

document_title: ACHE Code of Ethics
notes: Amended by Board of Governors November 13, 2017. Adherence is a membership requirement. Covers relationships with colleagues, patients, organization, community, society. 3 fundamental objectives of healthcare leadership profession.

document_title: Shared Code of Conduct for Registered Health Practitioners
notes: Shared by 12 of 15 National Boards. Medical, Nursing/Midwifery, Psychology Boards have profession-specific codes. Defines expected professional behaviour for registered health practitioners.

organization: National Association of Directors of Nursing Administration in Long Term Care
document_title: NADONA Code of Ethics
notes: Covers nursing administration in long-term care residential settings. Promotes quality of care for individuals receiving and delivering long-term care.

document_title: Code of Ethics and Standards of Practice for Aging Life Care Professionals
profession_name: Aging Life Care Professional/Geriatric Care Manager
notes: Originally 1990 (as NAPGCM); name changed 2015; most recent revision June 2025. Professional Conduct Review Committee enforces. Covers geriatric care management in residential/home settings.

organization: National Association for Home Care & Hospice
document_title: Code of Ethics
notes: Adopted September 1982 by NAHC Board of Directors. 8 sections: patient rights, agency-patient relationships, inter-agency cooperation, referrals, staffing, ethical financial practices, marketing, community service. Ethics Committee handles breaches.

organization: American Association on Intellectual and Developmental Disabilities
document_title: Guidelines to Professional Conduct
notes: First adopted 2012 by Board of Directors; revised January 29, 2020. Covers professionals serving individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities in residential and community settings.

document_title: Code of Ethics
notes: First approved 1960; 2021 revision adds professional self-care, updates cultural competence standard. 150+ specific guidelines across 6 areas. Most widely used US social work ethics code.

organization: International Federation of Social Workers / International Association of Schools of Social Work
document_title: Global Social Work Statement of Ethical Principles
notes: Approved at General Meetings in Dublin, July 2018. Replaces 2004 Ethics in Social Work Statement of Principles. Covers digital technology ethics, human rights, social justice. National associations develop specific codes from this framework.

document_title: Code of Ethics for Social Work
notes: In place since 1975; 2021 refreshed version. Binding on all BASW members in all roles across UK. Emphasizes human rights, social justice, professional integrity, anti-oppressive practice.

document_title: Code of Ethics
notes: November 2020 revision. 3 core values (simplified from previous edition). Part of regulatory suite with Australian Social Work Education and Accreditation Standards.

document_title: Code of Ethics, Values and Guiding Principles
notes: Released January 8, 2024. 7 values incorporating Truth and Reconciliation principles and Indigenous rights (new). Developed with input from ~2,000 members.

document_title: Ethical Standards for Human Service Professionals
notes: 2024 revision; previous version 2015. 44 standards in 7 areas: clients, colleagues, profession, public/society, employers, self, students. Addresses technology, telehealth, social media additions.
